svg.title: TOPAK H4 — The reference implementation, as deployed in development
svg.desc: mechanism/ runs the admit path end to end for Build's six actions and Run's three, an operator's six signed control actions, an emergency seating's activation and, since 2026.10.08, workflows and meshes run by the mechanism: three replicas of one Rust binary, an MCP front door on stdio, an operator socket, a linked Cedar floor (since 2026.10.08 the proposed floor's workflow stage, which is not in force), an OPA sidecar with a WASM fallback, and Kafka or an in-memory transport. It was rebuilt on 2026.10.05 in five stages, to labels and handles, the tool list, the operator as a principal and the emergency seating, and built on 2026.10.08 to two records that are Proposed, ADR-0054 and ADR-0055. It carries a launcher, a Run tool host and the operator path that the dev configuration does not turn on. It is evidence, not the verified object.
svg.text: TOPAK · H4

text.tspan: The reference implementation, as deployed in development

svg.text: mechanism/ runs the admit path end to end for Build's six actions and Run's three, an operator's six signed control actions, an emergency seating's activation and, since 2026.10.08, workflows and meshes run by the mechanism: three replicas of one Rust binary, an MCP front door on stdio, an operator socket, a linked Cedar floor (since 2026.10.08 the proposed floor's workflow stage, which is not in force), an OPA sidecar with a WASM fallback,

and Kafka or an in-memory transport. It was rebuilt on 2026.10.05 in five stages, to labels and handles, the tool list, the operator as a principal and the emergency seating, and built on 2026.10.08 to two records that are Proposed, ADR-0054 and ADR-0055. It carries a launcher, a Run tool host and the operator path that the dev configuration does not turn on. It is evidence, not the verified object.

text.tspan: Built at reference · evidence · rung 0 as deployed

svg.text: Rung 0 as deployed: the dev configuration has no contain section, so every lease it issues is rung 0. And no operator: the dev rules declare no operator or emergency seat, so the socket is D-0050-1, unsigned as before (I47 (b)); the operator path and the emergency seating run in the tests. In its tests the launcher (ADR-0033 A7, Batch 29) issues rung 1 on profiles that declare P3 fail, and rung 3 only SIMULATED under test keys: every principal it serves in earnest is Mediated; it

fails assumption of use A1, and no containment theorem describes it. Never promoted: no promotion pipeline exists, and nothing in it is in any TCB. Dev rules are not genesis rules: dev-init.sh generates keys and writes their secrets to dev/secrets/ in the clear (G6).

Cited like a TLA+ check, by manifest and commit: SHA256SUMS-REF-2026.10.09, digest 809c66beda3cdc6a, 116 entries, at 749d54f (ADR-0033 A17, pending; the trees below). It fails two entries at today's tree, and should: the pin file and the register moved after it (G11 §9). The last tree under a ratified addendum is 075b2e7 (A15, Batch 35). A running program invites being mistaken for the mechanism (ToO §15).

text.tspan: Rebuilt on 2026.10.05 in five stages, each its own commit and addendum (ADR-0033 A9 to A15; G10 §3); built to two Proposed records on 2026.10.08 (A16, A17; G11 §3)

For two days the reference followed records that were not in force and did not follow one that was, ADR-0013's X1; Batch 34 ended that by ratifying the records, two of them provisional (ToO §15; G10 §4). Each stage's floor was gated on 2026.10.04 (floor/proposed/<stage>-gates-results-2026.10.04.txt, every gate passing); the stage is genesis-provisional (ADR-0030 A3), and its files open with a comment, "not what the reference follows", that is wrong and kept as gated (item 91). Since
2026.10.08 it follows Proposed records again, at the custodian's direction, and links a stage that is not the floor in force (G11 item 102).
Any MCP-capable agent. Byzantine at every position (ADR-0007).
Launches topak mcp --socket dev/run/n1/agent.sock --token <token> --domain build|run as
its MCP server.
Not confined: an agent process with a shell, a network stack or a filesystem bypasses the front door entirely
(G1, the sandbox gap). A guest the node launches is the other way in: no token, stdio only (C5).
One process per session; crate topak-mcp (rmcp server), inside the topak binary.
Its tools are exactly the seat's alphabet: Build's six (ADR-0022 §1) or Run's three (ADR-0040 §1). Each call
becomes one typed action; unknown or malformed calls are errors, never a default.
It grants nothing: every call is decided by the replica.
MCP over stdio
topak op --socket dev/run/n1/operator.sock '{"op": …}', one JSON line in, one out.
Two paths share the socket (ADR-0050, provisional). control is an operator's request, signed with an
operator seat's key and decided by C1 to C9. Everything else is unsigned, from whoever reaches the socket
(file mode 0600). Where the rules declare an operator, that is a BOOTSTRAP path: grant and launch
make a first seating, standing in for the quorum, and the other unsigned requests are refused at apply.
Where they declare none, as the dev rules do, it is D-0050-1 (I47).

text.tspan: Environment steps, and an operator's signed requests

svg.text: run/n1/agent.sock, mode 0660; a bearer token names seat, lease, epoch; a launched lease mints none
run/n1/operator.sock, mode 0600
the eight steps of D1, in topak-node over topak-core
topak-floor: Cedar linked, the workflow stage (10ea6818af9b4efe, schema fd394bb8c074eec2), not in force; refuses to start unless the floor, schema and
values bytes match the gated digests. Its 123 cases replay through it. The floor in force is the emergency stage, genesis-provisional
topak-bundle: loads bundles_dir only under signatures verifying against bundle_keys, and only with a well-formed allowlist (W1 to W9, reading the two
issued lists once, from the genesis rules); one file that fails stops the node; sidecar client, WASM fallback
The deciding replica computes a call's label facts from the entry and the round; the admit carries them; apply folds them on every replica and re-checks only that
clearSet has not grown. A handle's result is held in memory by the replica that ran the call, dropped at the seal (I46)
Rendered at grant from the lease's revision and written as the round topic's first record, kind open, before the session exists; no record, no session (I45)
An operator's request: signature, counter and thirteen facts checked by every replica; a Regrant keeps the seating's binding and never widens; control records on
the operator's round topic, kind control (I47)
Distinct roster keys counted against the issued quorum on every replica; the envelope computed by the ordering replica; the person signs each action, no bearer
token (I48)
drive_workflows proposes each ready slot's grant; a route is checked again at apply; a node's attributes are lifted once when its round ends on its outcome; a
clear input is the predecessor's reports from this replica's own cache (finding 23). Proposed records (I49)
topak-paxos driven by driver.rs: persists fsynced before any send
run/n1/wal.jsonl: promises and accepted votes, durable before replies
every 250 ms, proposes EndRound(Expired) for leases this replica saw expire; since 7d8c7db a grant's observation is recorded before the state lock is released
workspaces/ (not replicated, G9); archive.jsonl, a projection of the log, not the archive; evidence/<digest>.json (I40); run/<seat>-e<epoch>-r<round>/
as a native Run tool's cwd
mechanism/launch.rs over topak-contain: launch, appraise, grant, bridge; renews against the same guest; destroys it when the round ends (A7). Off in dev: no
contain section
topak-contain wasmtool: a Wasm module per call whose one network capability is the target its allowlist entry declares in the lease's revision (A8, A9). None in
dev: wasm_tools is empty

text.tspan: Paxos over TCP among n1, n2, n3

svg.text: Unauthenticated JSON frames over plain TCP, best-effort: Paxos tolerates loss, duplication and reordering (net.rs). PROVISIONAL (replica authentication): mutual TLS is required before this
leaves a lab (G5; T-0045-1).
Fault model: crash-recovery, not Byzantine (ADR-0033 §3). A compromised replica could propose admits no floor evaluated.
No snapshots and no compaction: the log, the chosen map, the dedupe set and the WAL grow without bound (G14). Every admit waits for a consensus round.
unix agent socket
unix operator
socket
docker compose up opa: host :18181 → container :8181, serving bundles/${TOPAK_BUNDLE}.tar.gz.
Optional: dev-init.sh --opa points every replica at it; without it, the local WASM engine only.
Its answer counts only from the lease's revision, and only if that revision verified (ADR-0044 §3).
Unpinned: latest here and in build-bundle.sh, which compiles the Rego to policy.wasm with the same image;
the signed revision hashes the source, not the module (inventory finding 11).
docker compose up kafka: :9092; dev-init.sh --kafka sets brokers 127.0.0.1:9092, replication 1.
Without it: in-memory transport. Round topics topak.<chain>.<domain>.<seat>.e<epoch>.r<round> and their
.after companions.
Transport only: ADR-0005, accepted in Batch 27, discharging the K row's debt (ADR-0033 §2). Record kinds open
(the tool list) and control join emit, actuate and deny.
Spawned per call by the tool host over stdio, as wordcount@<digest>; digest = SHA-256(binary digest ‖ canonical
JSON of its MCP input schema), both halves checked on every call.
Cleared environment, the workspace as working directory, and nothing more: hermeticity is unchecked (G4), and a
native Run tool's channel is checked by nobody (G19). A Run tool hosted as Wasm reaches only the target its entry
declares (I44); dev hosts none. ADR-0049 §2's digest over the entry's inputs is not followed (I13; item 94).
build-bundle.sh: policies/ → OPA WASM bundles/<revision>.tar.gz; revision = SHA-256 over sorted
non-test .rego and data.json (since A10 3e98ed176ba6c339): the source. policy.wasm is whatever the unpinned
OPA produced. data.json holds the allowlist in ADR-0049's five-part form; two comments there still call ADR-0049
Proposed, and changing them is a new bundle (item 98).
dev-init.sh signs a copy into dev/bundles/ with <revision>.sig under a dev bundle key whose public half the
rules carry in bundle_keys; the tracked tarball stays unsigned. Signing at promotion is a script step (G7 item 67).

text.tspan: Timers and limits: the reference's, named by no record (inventory §5.6, §9)

svg.text: heartbeat_ms 50 · election_timeout_ms 400 in the node's config (the crate's own default is 300, reachable only from its tests; finding 22) · max_catchup 256 · frames: MAX_FRAME 64 MiB, connect 200
ms, per-peer queue 4096, dropping when full
COMMIT_DEADLINE 5 s · RETRY_EVERY 750 ms · driver tick 10 ms · expiry sweep 250 ms · channels: proposals 1024, inbound 8192, launcher control 8
opa_timeout_ms 250 · hello_timeout_ms 10000 · launcher renewal every ttl_ms / 2 with a fresh nonce · guest-io buffer 64 lines
FUEL 50,000,000 · NET_TIMEOUT 2 s · one fresh instance per call (I44)
One JSON line per persisted Paxos output; append-only, fsync per batch, replay stops at a torn line, never compacted (G14)
{slot, entry, applied} per line; truncated at startup and rebuilt: a projection, not the archive (G9)
ws-<seat>-e<epoch>-r<round>/ for Draft; run/<seat>-e<epoch>-r<round>/ as a native Run tool's cwd; neither replicated
Appraisal evidence the launcher retained (I40), named by its canonical digest and written non-canonically, so the file's own SHA-256 is not its name (inventory finding 13)

topak check-rules validates rules.json against the rules floor at the end of dev-init.sh, and every replica refuses rules that violate it at startup: the runtime stand-in for the unwritten GenesisSatisfiesFloor.

text.tspan: The wire formats, as the reference serializes them: no record defines any of these
, mode 0660; one JSON line each way; PROVISIONAL (session binding), I14

svg.text: {"token": <64 hex>, "op": "act", "action": <Action>}; or {"op": "submit_workspace"} (the node computes the workspace
digest, I12); or {"op": "abstain"} (refused for Run seats, I31)
{"admitted": bool, "detail": …}; detail is {"decision": "deny", "reason": <DenyReason>}, {"decision": "admit",
"slot", "floor": [@ids], "engine", "result"}, {"abstained": true} or {"error"}
{"token", "op": "tool_list"}: no admit, the same answer all round, {"tool_list": {digest, list}}. The list is the canonical
JSON of {bundle, domain, tools}, each tool's name, digest, purpose, inputs and notes, and in Run its labels and {kind, outward}
without the target (I45)
Read, Consult: {object, content} · Draft: {written, digest} · Invoke: the tool's CallToolResult, or the Wasm tool's JSON ·
Actuate: {topic, offset, seq, outcome, result_digest, result}, or after a seal {seq, outcome: "unknown", withheld} ·
Emit, Report: {topic, offset, seq} · Submit: {submitted} · Vote: {recorded, artifact, promoted}
32 random bytes as hex, minted by the applying replica into a per-replica sessions map as {seat, fence, epoch}; not replicated;
renew moves its fence; a launched lease mints none
topak mcp maps each tool to an AgentOp by adding kind: Build read{object}, draft{target, content}, invoke{tool, digest,
inputs}, emit{record}, submit{artifact?}, abstain{}, vote{verdict, artifact, evidence, rules_epoch}; Run consult,
actuate, report. Every input schema is a closed object; the result is one text block holding detail; protocol version 2025-06-18. At
start it asks for the tool list and puts it in the server's instructions, "the only description of them with standing"

text.tspan: , mode 0600, PROVISIONAL (operator authentication); plain TCP among replicas, PROVISIONAL (replica

svg.text: {"op": <name>, …} with the fields the table at left names: grant takes principal, seat, persona, bundle,
confinement{digest, rung}, alphabet[], ttl_ms, round, role, and optionally task_label, task_labels_allowed, sign_on;
launch takes profile in place of persona and confinement; revoke takes target{kind, id}, reason, attribution; issue an
{"op": "control", "request": {operator, epoch, ctr, action, …}, "sig": {key, sig}, "assertion"?, "task"?},
signed over {chain, request}; {"op": "activate", "activation", "approvals": [Signed], "task"?}; {"op":
"prepare_emergency", "seat", "seating"}. A successful grant, regrant or activation returns the tool_list and the task as
delivered
{ok, slot, applied: <Applied>}, or {ok: false, error} after the 5 s deadline. grant adds fence, token, lease,
contained, because; launch adds verdict, rung, instance, evidence, simulated, or {ok: false, verdict: refused |
unattestable | contested, …}; status returns {replica, chain, leader, last_applied, epoch, rules_epoch, floor,
schema, params, live_leases[], candidates[], launched[]}: the floor and schema digests, not the values file's (inventory
finding 12)
LeaseGranted{fence}, Renewed{fence}, Admitted{seq, promoted}, RoundEnded, Revoked{ended}, EpochIncremented{epoch},
Contested{ended}, ProfileRegistered{digest}, Issued{rules_epoch}, GatesRecorded, EmergencyPrepared,
WorkflowLoaded{workflow}, WorkflowFailed{reason}, BreakGlassApproved{approvals} (which no entry can now produce),
Rejected(String), Duplicate
A big-endian u32 length, then the JSON of [from_node_id, <Msg<Entry>>]: Prepare, Promise, Nack, Accept, Accepted, Commit,
Heartbeat, CatchUp, Forward (topak-paxos). Unauthenticated, best-effort
Signed = {key, sig} (Ed25519, hex) over "topak/<purpose>/v1\n" ‖ canonical JSON; purposes issuance, bundle, appraisal,
agent-op, sim-report, key, and since 10.05 control, sign-on and emergency-activation; break-glass is refused. Canonical
JSON: keys sorted recursively, no whitespace, sorted by hand because cedar-policy-core turns on preserve_order (register finding
input_len() -> i32, input_read(ptr), output(ptr, len), connect() -> handle | -1, send(h, ptr, len), recv(h, ptr,
cap). Any other import is refused at load and the node does not start
memory and run() -> i32 (0 is ok). Input is the inputs map as JSON; output must be JSON, empty meaning null
connect reaches only the {kind, target} the tool's allowlist entry declares in the bundle revision the lease names, handed to the host
with each call; no address crosses the boundary. An entry with no channel in that revision is not run. ChannelUse{connects, sent,
received} is returned to the caller and recorded nowhere
WasmToolSpec = {module, module_sha256} under the node's wasm_tools, keyed name@<module sha256>: where the module is and
what its bytes are, and no channel since 7764e52; FUEL 50,000,000, NET_TIMEOUT 2 s, one fresh instance per call. The entry is the only
declaration (A9; item 84 closed)
ToolSpec = {command, args[], binary_sha256, mcp_tool} under tools, keyed name@digest with digest = SHA-256(
binary_sha256 ‖ 0x00 ‖ canonical MCP input schema) (I13); every call re-hashes the binary, lists tools, recomputes the digest, then
makes one call

text.tspan: How it is checked, and how it stays honest

svg.text: mutations.rs (36), confinement.rs (19), operators.rs (6), emergency.rs (5), workflow.rs (18), drift.rs (2)
(core); sim.rs (4, Paxos with Voting invariants); floor.rs (5, the stage's cases), workflow.rs (3) (floor);
allowlist.rs (13, W1 to W10), fallback.rs (10) (bundle tier); e2e.rs (10), contain.rs (14) (node); launch.rs
(6), wasmtool.rs (4) (topak-contain).
TLA+ properties restated as Rust tests with the same mutations; run on a copy of the tree at 11aaf6a (A16) and at
749d54f (A17), 155 passing.
TOPAK_TRACE_DIR makes every apply write a step: index, entry, result and a projected state (trace.rs).
trace2tla.py converts; mechanism-trace-run.sh replays in TLC.
2026.10.05 (A14): 82 traces, 1,007 steps, every step matching, each state also read against Confinement_A1's
invariants; the model broken on purpose five ways, each caught, and a sixth as an evaluation error. It found the race
in lease expiry. A mechanized link, not a refinement; T-0045-28 stays a trust root. Not rerun since: the model does
not cover workflows (A16). The Lean models of apply replay the same traces, and are stale since the workflow build

text.tspan: Corpus pins and the drift test

svg.text: corpus-pins.sha256: 61 pins, 42 records and 19 TLA+ modules the reference follows.
cargo test -p topak-core --test drift fails when a pinned file changes, or when the code cites a record that
is not pinned. PROVISIONAL (<tag>) is meant to mark every gap in the code, and the register says it does; two
items carry no tag (I40 evidence retention, I41 session proof) and two sites a bare PROVISIONAL: (inventory finding
scripts/smoke.py: processes, TCP, operator CLI and an MCP client, in-memory or against Kafka and the sidecar.
Not rerun since 2026.09.25 (G7 item 52), and as written it would fail at its grant line: it reads a note key the grant
reply does not have (inventory finding 19).

text.tspan: What it does not show (ToO rev 15 §15; ADR-0033 §6, A11, A12, A16; the register at G11)
What stands in, and what that leaves

svg.text: The launcher makes the alphabet the whole channel for a guest it starts; no guest it starts passes P3, no host it runs on attests (rung 3 is SIMULATED, rung 2 a seam), and an agent outside a launcher still has a shell
G1; items 34, 36
Tools are pinned by binary and schema and run in a cleared environment; their behaviour is unchecked
G4

A Wasm-hosted Run tool reaches only its declared target; a native one is checked by nobody, the channel is declared twice and not checked to agree, and a P4-pass Build profile is not held to Wasm tools
G19; items 83, 84
One is seated, its heartbeats are heard and its absence stalls; the Observer that would produce a finding is an e2e fixture with nothing behind it

text.tspan: A first lease from a quorum

svg.text: The centre of ADR-0050, which is why it is provisional. The BOOTSTRAP path stands in: whoever reaches the socket can seat. The first operators from an anchor issuance are not built either (G11 §8)
I47; item 88

prepare_emergency is the BOOTSTRAP path, unsigned, standing in for it; ADR-0052 stays provisional on it and on two questions the reference raised: whether operators' seatings feed the emergency envelope, and whether a delivery table needs an emergency row
I48; item 92

text.tspan: A socket path for a person's signed action

svg.text: The agent socket's protocol carries no proof, so an emergency seat acts in-process, as the tests do. The drill is on the log and nothing counts it
I48; item 92
An operator's Persona is its seat's key: no Persona record, no lineage. A Regrant that would launch a guest is not built; Launch and RegisterProfile are still unsigned
I47; item 88

The label facts and an activation's envelope are the deciding replica's; a failed call's error text reaches the principal unlabelled; a handle resolves only to a scalar, from results one replica holds in memory
I46; item 93

text.tspan: What the records in force ask that it does not do

svg.text: ADR-0049 §2's digest over the entry's inputs; a task at a first seating, and so its label; the two issued lists re-read when an issuance changes them
I13, I46; item 94
ADR-0051 is Proposed, Correlator.tla proved and certified; nothing at the reference
item 97

text.tspan: Workflows as an occupant would run them

svg.text: The cells are the tests', handed sessions by workflow_status; a finding's form is the reference's; lineage is a declared tag; a clear input arrives only from the replica that served its predecessor, and a handle input cannot be resolved; a seating above rung 0 and an all join in a mesh do not load; no T_wf or step bound; no pools, parity seatings or
fan-out-scoped joins. The records are Proposed, and the floor stage is not in force
Cells are declared, not enforced. Operators and emergency seats add readers that nothing gates: the mechanism has no read path for topics
I8; item 46

text.tspan: The archive and the plaintext store

svg.text: archive.jsonl per replica is a projection of the log; no governed store, no horizon, no audit-authority read path
G9
Not implemented; no erasure roster exists, so X2-erasure admits nothing
Wrapper-Rego masking (ADR-0003 0003.6) is not built
ToO §15
For an operator grant, persona is an operator-supplied digest; a launch's appraisal must name the profile's, which is all the rung detects
Dev rules, not genesis rules; no anchor ceremony
G6
None; scale and long-running behaviour are not shown

text.tspan: Replica authentication; operators where none is declared

svg.text: Plain TCP between replicas; socket file modes and bearer tokens. An operator's request is signed only where the rules declare an operator seat
A script step under a dev key with custody (1, 0); no pipeline, no custody row
G7 item 67

text.tspan: That the floor is the right floor

svg.text: Floor fitness is owned and timed, with no test: the bootstrap reviewer establishes it and the floor is ratified with that (ADR-0030 A3); what makes a floor fit is not written
G16; items 2, 87

The rung-1 launcher, a SIMULATED rung 3, the session proof, Contained as a lookup, and the Run tool host for Wasm modules, under A7 and A8 (ratified in Batches 29 and 31); the launcher's ADR-0036 is still Proposed

Labels and handles, the tool list, the allowlist entry, the operator principal and the emergency seating, under A9 to A15 (Batches 32 to 35), two on provisional records, on a genesis-provisional floor
Workflows and meshes, under A16 and A17, both pending, to records that are Proposed, on a floor stage that is not in force
the mechanism (replica, front door)
consensus (P), checks
bundle tier, transport
operator, tools, dev config
agent
not built, residual
